item.title: Funding announced for Elphin Windmill welcomed locally
item.description: Elphin Windmill has been allocated funding under the Heritage Investment Scheme. From rural areas and rural villages, the scheme helps protect historic structures, enhance streetscapes and keep traditional building skills alive for future generations. The sails were torn off the 300-year-old structure during the deadly Storm Éowyn. It has been a popular tourist attraction since it was restored almost 30 years ago. item.title: Local priest says schools play a huge role in keeping religion alive
item.description: A local priest says schools play a huge role in keeping religion alive in 2026. Local schools in the Shannonside region have been celebrating Catholic Schools week in many different ways. Ardagh/Moydow priest Fr. Vinny Connaughton has been visiting schools across the region and this morning he held a service for the students of Glen National School and their grandparents. He said weeks and events like this are crucial for keeping young people engaged in religion: Advertisement

item.title: Devastation 'still being felt' on one-year anniversary of Storm Éowyn
item.description: The devastation from Storm Éowyn is still being felt on its one year anniversary today. Over eight hundred thousand homes were left without power and over one hundred thousand without water. Cavan Monaghan Fianna Fail TD Brendan Smith says the electricity grid needs to have greater resilience and telecom providers must also strengthen their networks. Deputy Smith says locals are still worried about steps that need to be taken a year on: Advertisement

item.title: No community welfare officer currently based in Castlerea
item.description: No community welfare officer is currently based in Castlerea, Co Roscommon. The Social Protection Minister has confirmed the news to a local TD. Independent Ireland's Michael Fitzmaurice asked Minister Dara Calleary why there's no community welfare officer, or CWO, in Castlerea. He called for the position to be filled. item.title: Over €370,000 secured for local heritage projects
item.description: Over €370,000 worth of funding has been announced for projects in the Shannonside region under the Built Heritage Investment Scheme. The funding is provided by the Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage's National Built Heritage Service. Roscommon received the highest allocation locally from this weeks funding announcement with over €140,000 going to projects in the county. item.title: Bluetongue animal case detected in Co. Wexford
item.description: Bluetongue has been detected in an animal in Co Wexford. The Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine, Martin Heydon, confirmed the outbreak, saying the news is unwelcome but not surprising as the virus has been spreading across Europe, Britain and Northern Ireland. The outbreak will have an impact on exports of cattle and sheep, with additional costs required in order to comply with the rules of the countries of destination. item.title: Over 10,000 criminal offences recorded locally in first nine months of 2025
item.description: Over 10,000 criminal offences were carried out in the Shannonside region in the first nine months of 2025. Figures published by the Central Statistics Office do show similar offences were carried out in both the Sligo-Leitrim and Roscommon-Longford Garda divisions. item.title: People in Longford Town look back on Storm Éowyn on one-year anniversary
item.description: Today marks one year since Storm Éowyn swept across the country and left over 800 thousand homes without power. The strongest storm to ever hit the country caused extensive damage to local parks and buildings, as well as a lack of water supply for over one hundred thousand people. The devastation from the storm is still being felt today, with Coillte estimating it won't be until 2027 before its clean-up operation is complete.
